title: ExtendScript files must stay ES3: guard them against the formatter and test their syntax
rule: A file that Adobe's ExtendScript engine loads (a CEP `jsx/*.jsx` ScriptPath) is ES3: no trailing commas, let/const, arrows, template literals, classes, JSON, spread, ES5 array methods or trim. The repo's Prettier formats plugins/ with trailingComma "all", so keep the `**/*.jsx` override (`trailingComma: none`) in .prettierrc.json, and give every such file a test that blanks comments and strings and rejects those forms. Tests that run the file in V8 (new Function) do not prove it loads in ExtendScript.
rationale: E30.2 (#188): Prettier added a trailing comma to a multi-line call in host.jsx; ES3 ExtendScript cannot parse it, so no host function would load in Illustrator and the extension would silently do nothing, while every V8-based test stayed green.
